szoveg_eredeti:
I built ManyAgents because I kept losing track of 10+ agents across projects. I'd love to learn how others handle it:

How many agents do you usually run at once, and across how many projects?

What breaks first: keeping track, merge conflicts, usage limits, or reviewing the work?

What would you pay for a tool like this: one-time, monthly, or not at all?

Every answer helps shape what I build next. Thanks!

I often have 10+ AI agents running at once: writing code, reviewing changes, running tests and coordinating the work. Across several projects that can triple, and keeping track of who's doing what gets overwhelming.

So I built ManyAgents, a Mac app where each project gets an orchestrator. It hands work to agents in their own git worktrees, has a reviewer check it, and lets them test their changes in a built-in browser beside the chat. Every question lands in one place.

It's free for 14 days. I'm still working out pricing, so I'd love to hear what you'd pay, and what's missing from how you run your agents today.

Weboldal: https://manyagents.app
